finding: For the unresolved minimal weak-certificate pattern with t1,t2 in odd band 1, t3,t4 in the next gap, and t5 in odd band 2, the existence of a single root xi in [t3,t4] whose Vieta cubic gives positive pairing on both odd circuits uniformly for every admissible even box and all actual odd choices is exactly one finite LP. Its variables are xi's affine parameter and four sets of nonnegative multipliers on six strict box-stability margins, four interval widths and four strictly positive lower coefficients. The forward direction uses Motzkin's strict linear alternative on the nonempty stable-box cone; the reverse gives an explicit certificate. Feasibility excludes the five-node weak no-go for those fixed odd data. Infeasibility only excludes this restricted uniform selector, not a box-dependent selector or general synthesis. Nonvacuity follows from the pinned strict dual example.

evidence.status: WRITTEN fixed-data LP equivalence; no general solver proof, independent review or parent adoption

remaining_gap: No proof that the selector LP is feasible for all odd data; no exact counterexample tuple; ten minimal phase words remain open in whole or part, as do larger supports and the original arbitrary-box synthesis question.
